MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "simple bone cyst"
- "AP (anteroposterior) X-ray of the proximal humerus, physis **open**: a **metaphyseal, central, osteolytic** lesion with **well-defined** margins."
- "The cortex shows **thinning** with mild expansion, not wider than the physis. A **fallen fragment** lies in the cavity. So → **benign active**."
- "In a child my differential is **simple bone cyst**, ABC (aneurysmal bone cyst), fibrous dysplasia, NOF (non-ossifying fibroma)."
- "Next → MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) only if in doubt; no biopsy. Treatment → humerus: observe or inject; fracture → sling, then reassess · **proximal femur → never leave → fix**."

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **5–20, male · central metaphysis, proximal humerus · fallen fragment · thin fibrous lining · observe / inject; femur → fix**

### 1 Definition
- Simple bone cyst (**unicameral bone cyst**, UBC; solitary bone cyst) → **benign latent** · unknown origin → one chamber, no septa; a **pseudo-cyst** with no epithelial or endothelial lining; reactive or developmental, not a true neoplasm

### 2 Origin
- **Unknown origin** in the Lichtenstein–Dahlin table, with ABC and GCT (giant cell tumour) → 1 Introduction · primary only; never with another lesion, unlike ABC

| Theory | Point |
|---|---|
| Blocked drainage (accepted) | Metaphyseal remodelling defect → interstitial fluid blocked → pressure → bone necrosis → fluid |
| Venous obstruction | Cyst pressure above marrow pressure; low oxygen tension in the fluid (Chigira 1983) |
| Fluid content | Prostaglandins, interleukins, cytokines, metalloproteinases → bone resorption |
| Trauma | Physeal injury in a child, no time for a lining — Prof Abosena's favourite |

### 3 Incidence
- **Age** → **First two decades** (85%), mostly 5–20 · **Sex** → **male : female = 2 : 1** · **Relative incidence** → **commonest bone lesion of the immature skeleton** · adult → rare, in odd sites: **calcaneus, ilium** (Campbell; OKU Tumors 4)

### 4 Sites
- **Longitudinal** → **Metaphyseal**, abutting the physis, moves toward the diaphysis with growth · **Transverse** → **central** · never epiphyseal, never through the cortex (Campbell)
- **Special sites** → **Proximal humerus > proximal femur**, together 90% · calcaneus 2–11% (Prof Abosena; OKU Tumors 4) · groups → **expansile lesions** → 1 Differential

- Sites, age and sex of SBC, diagram (Greenspan)

### 5 Clinical presentation
| Local | Systemic | Complications by location |
|---|---|---|
| **Asymptomatic**, found after a minor fall | None | Proximal femur → neck fracture, **AVN** (avascular necrosis), growth arrest |
| Pain with a fracture or an impending fracture | — | Calcaneus → intra-articular fracture, hard to treat |

- **Complications** → **Pathological fracture** → first sign in **two-thirds** (Campbell)
- Three scenarios (Prof Abosena) → **accidental discovery** (humerus: leave · femur: intervene) · **pain or swelling** · **pathological fracture**

### 6 Imaging
| Frame A step | Textbooks |
|---|---|
| Site | Metaphysis next to the physis (active) or proximal diaphysis (latent) |
| Centralization · behavior | **Central** · purely osteolytic, no matrix |
| Margins | Well-defined, thin sclerotic rim; ridges look multiloculated (pseudosepta) |
| Cortical reaction | Thinning, mild expansion **not wider than the physis**; **no periosteal reaction unless fractured** |
| Special signs | **Fallen fragment (fallen leaf)** sign |

- Classic films: proximal humerus, humeral shaft, proximal femur (Prof Abosena)

PITFALL — bone scan hot or cold?
- Handbook → "hot until skeletal maturity, cold after" · OKU Tumors 4 → **peripheral uptake, central photopenia**; Greenspan → ring uptake, not specific
- Say → "**rim uptake, cold centre**; a bone scan is not needed for SBC"

### 7 Labs
- **Routine** → **Basic labs only** · **Specific** → weak-looking bone, several cysts, generalised pain → serum **parathormone** + vitamin D (brown tumour) (Prof Abosena)

### 8 Biopsy
- **Modality** → **No biopsy** for a classic cyst (Prof Abosena) · **straw-coloured** fluid at injection confirms it
- **Gross** → clear yellow serous fluid; blood only after a fracture · **microscopic** → thin fibrous lining (<1 mm) of fibroblasts, scattered giant cells, haemosiderin; fibrinoid "cementum" (Campbell)

- SBC histology, H&E (Rosario 2017, open access)

Key exclusion → **solid tissue** in the cavity means not SBC; curettage yields almost none

### 9 Differential diagnosis
- **Location groups** → **By location** → central metaphysis of a child: SBC, fibrous dysplasia, enchondroma; calcaneus: SBC, intraosseous lipoma · **by cortex** → expansile lesions → 1 Differential · **by cell** → not a giant-cell lesion, though scattered giant cells line it
- **Special DD** → **The mimic** → **ABC** (twins table below) · bone abscess (periosteal reaction, crosses the physis) · NOF

- Film beside film: SBC humerus | NOF | bone abscess (Greenspan)

| Film | Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SBC | metaphyseal + diaphyseal | central | osteolytic | well-defined | thinning | none | **benign latent** |
| NOF | metaphyseal + diaphyseal | eccentric | osteolytic | well-defined | thinning + expansion | none | **benign latent** |
| Bone abscess | metaphyseal + epiphyseal | central | osteolytic | well-defined | periosteal reaction | crosses the physis | **benign active** |

### 10 Grading
- **Benign stage** → **Benign latent** (Enneking 1); quiet at maturity · **active vs latent** by distance from the physis · healing → shrinks, edges sclerose, septa appear, cyst "migrates" — only apparent: the physis outgrows it

| | Active | Latent |
|---|---|---|
| Distance from physis | **Within 1 cm** (Campbell) | Farther; into the diaphysis |
| Age · cortex | Younger child · thinned, expanded, may fracture | Older child · not thinned |
| Outcome | Recurs more; worse after any treatment | Better; >2 cm from the physis heals better |

| Outcome after treatment (Prof Abosena) | Definition |
|---|---|
| Healed | Whole cyst filled with new bone |
| Healed with defect | Residual defect <50% of bone diameter |
| Persistent | >50% of diameter; thin cortical rim |
| Recurrent | Reappeared at the original size |

### 11 Treatment
- **Benign** → Small, asymptomatic, upper limb → **observation** · large, painful, lower limb → **injection** or **curettage** ± graft ± fixation
- **Proximal femur** → curettage, graft and internal fixation · recurrent after 3 injections → curettage + graft · poor-prognosis cysts → multiloculated, large, active, **age <10** (Campbell)

CLINICAL PEARL — follow the wall, not the cavity (Prof Abosena)
- Judge the **cyst wall** and the symptoms: sclerotic wall → reassure; thin wall → fracture risk · asymptomatic → review every 3 months

**Injection protocol** (Campbell)
1) Sedation or anaesthesia; two 18-gauge needles under fluoroscopy, one at each end
2) **Straw-coloured fluid** confirms the diagnosis; cystogram with contrast
3) **Methylprednisolone 80–200 mg**, by age and cyst size
4) No healing at

EXAM PEARL — The examiner asks

CLINICAL PEARL — cement and the physis (Prof Abosena)
- Cement in a child → only **away from the physis**; forced near it → sponge or iliac graft over the physis, cement above

| Option | Point |
|---|---|
| **Sclerotherapy** | Polidocanol, alcohol, doxycycline; repeated; polidocanol ≈ surgery in one trial |
| Embolisation | First for an intact spinal ABC; repeat every 8 weeks until healing (Amendola 2013) |
| **Denosumab** | Anti-RANKL (receptor activator of nuclear factor-κB ligand), off-label for inoperable ABC; 120 mg days 1, 8, 15, 29, then every 4 weeks; recurrence after stopping, **hypercalcaemia** 6 months after stopping (Dürr 2019) |
| Radiotherapy | Not routine → growth arrest, malignant change |
| Ethibloc | A fatal vertebrobasilar embolisation after a C2 injection |

EXAM PEARL — The examiner asks
- **Phases of ABC?** → initial osteolytic · growth · stabilisation · healing
- **Capanna types?** → I central contained · II central expansile · III eccentric (commonest) · IV subperiosteal · V periosteal
- **Why operate at once?** → aggressive, grows fast (growth phase), destroys bone and physis, fractures; sarcoma not excluded without tissue
- **Recurrence by age?** → highest **≤5 years** (5 of 9), lower >10 years; <15 years a risk factor

| The examiner asks (Prof Abosena's Q&A) | Short answer |
|---|---|
| Fractured ABC → biopsy or fix first? | Biopsy (CT-guided core) → wait for result → fix; not the same sitting |
| Biopsy delays a child's care? | Open biopsy + frozen section with the pathologist present; rare |
| Cement in children? | Not routine; recurrent large ABC after embolisation; protect the physis |
| ABC treatment after biopsy? | Extended curettage · en bloc if large and recurrent · cryotherapy then curettage |
| Filler after curettage? | Nothing, fibula, bone substitute, or cement (mature only) |

4.03.b:
| # | Simple bone cyst | Aneurysmal bone cyst |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Definition | **Benign latent**; unicameral, fluid | **Benign aggressive**; multilocular, blood |
| 2 Origin | Primary only | Primary 70% (USP6) · secondary 30% |
| 3 Incidence | 5–20 · **male 2 : 1** | <20 · **slight female** |
| 4 Sites | Proximal humerus, proximal femur · **central** | Proximal humerus, distal femur, proximal tibia, spine · **eccentric** |
| 5 Clinical | Asymptomatic → **fracture** | **Pain + swelling** |
| 6 Imaging | Not wider than physis · **fallen fragment** · no periosteal reaction | **Wider than physis** · buttress · **fluid–fluid levels** |
| 7 Labs | Basic | Basic; parathormone if bone looks weak |
| 8 Biopsy | **No** | **Mandatory** |
| 9 Differential | ABC, fibrous dysplasia, NOF, abscess | **Telangiectatic osteosarcoma**, GCT, CMF, SBC |
| 10 Grading | Active (≤1 cm) / latent | Capanna I–V · phases 1–4 |
| 11 Treatment | Observe · **inject** · femur → fix (Miller) | **Extended curettage** · embolise · sclerotherapy (Miller) |
| 12 Prognosis | Recurrence after surgery ≈50% (old), 88% if <10 + active | Recurrence 10–20%; ≤5 years worst |

- Cyst **wider than the physis** → ABC · not wider → SBC (Miller)
